## Acknowledgements and sources

This package is part of an inference suite (infercalcR, inferguidR and
infereportR) that is deeply inspired by DescrTab2 [1], developed at the
Institute of Medical Biometry (IMBI), Heidelberg University, by Jan Meis, Lukas
Baumann, Maximilian Pilz and Lukas Sauer. Its test-choice tree, its validation
statement and its practice of computing each test with an established
implementation are the model for how the suite chooses, computes and reports
statistical tests. DescrTab2 was archived on CRAN on 18 October 2025; its source
code remains available on GitHub. The methods-consulting pages of the University
of Zurich [2], with their decision tree, decision assistant, worked examples and
explanations, inspired the guidance in the suite. Power and sample-size planning
and the distribution calculator follow G\*Power 3.1 [3, 4]. We thank the authors
of these works for making them openly available. The [package
README](https://github.com/CTTIR/inferguidR#acknowledgements-and-sources) cites
all software the package uses.

1. Meis J, Baumann L, Pilz M, Sauer L (2022). *DescrTab2: Publication Quality Descriptive Statistics Tables*. R package version 2.1.16. <https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.DescrTab2>. Source code, including the development version 2.1.26: <https://github.com/imbi-heidelberg/DescrTab2>.
2. Universität Zürich, Methodenberatung. *Datenanalyse mit SPSS*: decision tree (Entscheidbaum), decision assistant (Entscheidassistent) and method pages with examples and explanations. <https://www.methodenberatung.uzh.ch/de/datenanalyse_spss.html>. Accessed 3 October 2026.
3. Faul F, Erdfelder E, Lang A-G, Buchner A (2007). G\*Power 3: A flexible statistical power analysis program for the social, behavioral, and biomedical sciences. *Behavior Research Methods*, 39(2), 175-191. <https://doi.org/10.3758/BF03193146>.
4. Faul F, Erdfelder E, Buchner A, Lang A-G (2009). Statistical power analyses using G\*Power 3.1: Tests for correlation and regression analyses. *Behavior Research Methods*, 41(4), 1149-1160. <https://doi.org/10.3758/BRM.41.4.1149>.
